title: Private deploy onboarding orchestration wizard — UX scenarios and backlog
content:
Context and goals:

This is a working doc to capture UX scenarios, edge cases and an initial groomed backlog for the Private Deployment onboarding/orchestration wizard. Target audience: product PMs, console UX, solutions and SEs who will run customer installs. Goal: build a single guided flow that reliably gets a customer from "intent to run private" -> network + region + key management configured -> validation checks -> deployment plan exported and kick-started.

Principles (working):
- Make the safest path the default: conservative network config that passes common enterprise audits.
- Surface tradeoffs (latency vs compliance vs cost) in plain language at decision points.
- Provide exportable artifacts (YAML config, audit checklist) so SEs and infra teams can review offline.
- Fail fast with actionable remediation steps and links to logs/support.
- Keep the flow short (3–6 screens) but allow deep dives per step.

High-level flow (user goals framed as tasks):
1) Declare deployment footprint: regions + availability expectations
   - Single region or multi-region? (tooltip: latency vs DR vs cost)
   - Map to cloud provider regions (UI shows approximate p99 latency hints to hosted regions).
2) Network setup: VPC, subnets, routing, NAT/IGW choices
   - Offer: "Use our recommended VPC" vs "Bring your own VPC"
   - If BYOVPC: guided checklist to validate subnets, route tables, NACLs, and peering/VPN connectivity.
   - Provide a connectivity test that runs in the background (shows progress + expected duration).
3) Identity & secrets: KMS vs HSM selection and key policies
   - Explain difference, compliance signals, and cost/latency implications.
content_continued:
(continued)
4) Capacity and instance selection: Dedicated pools, reserved capacity hints, autoscaling policy stub
   - Show estimated token cost per 1k qps for suggested instance types.
5) Validation and policy checks: security scans, region compliance mapping, firewall tests
   - Failure modes surfaced with remediation steps and auto-suggested fixes where possible.
6) Review & export: YAML manifest, audit checklist, support bundle
   - One-click start or schedule maintenance window.

Wireframe and microcopy notes:
- Landing card copy: "Bring Redwood Private online in your VPC — guided setup in 6 steps (takes ~20–40 mins depending on network checks)."
- CTA variants: "Start guided setup" (primary), "Upload prepared manifest" (secondary).
- Step header style: short goal line + single-sentence explanation + learn-more link (links to Confluence).

Network step micro-interactions and edge cases:
- When user selects BYOVPC, immediately show a read-only checklist with green/red items based on API validation: subnets reachable? route to NAT? CIDR overlap?
- If CIDR overlap detected: show suggested ranges and an option to continue with NAT translation workaround (warn about increased complexity).
- Peering vs Transit Gateway messaging: default to peering for single-region installs; surface TGW for >2 regions or multi-account setups with diagram.
- Allow uploading a screenshot or transcript from customer network team and attach as "notes for SE".

KMS/HSM decision matrix (UX framing):
- Quick-mode toggle: "Compliance-first (HSM)" vs "Latency/cost-first (KMS)"
- When HSM selected, show: required hardware modules in region (if not available, show alternatives or managed HSM partners), expected key-per-ops latency delta, and procurement checklist.
- Insist on explicit key rotation policy selection: auto-rotate (recommended) vs customer-managed schedule.
- If HSM not available in chosen region, show inline migration workaround: provision keys in neighboring region + cross-region replication policy (with explicit compliance caveats).

Validation checks and remediation UX patterns:
- Run incremental checks after each major step rather than a monolithic final check. This reduces time to detect issues.
- For failing checks, present: 1) clear failure title, 2) likely cause, 3) quick fix (1–2 steps), 4) fallback (e.g., choose hosted routing for initial launch), 5) attach logs button that collects debug zip for support.
- Example failure: "VPC route table missing route to NAT" -> quick fix: add route (inline edit) or switch to our recommended VPC.

Operator flows and recovery scenarios (important for SEs):
- Interrupted setup (browser closed, network hiccup): persist state server-side and show resume link in Console -> Private Deployments -> Active Setups. Include a "continue as different user" option with audit log.
- Partial deploy (services installed but health checks failing): offer a staged rollback to pre-deploy snapshot or a targeted re-run of failed steps. Provide clear visibility into which infra pieces are in which state.
- Upgrade path from Dedicated-hosted to Private: export manifest, run preflight, confirm resource mappings. Show a migration impact summary (downtime, cost delta, rollback plan).

Accessibility and internationalization notes:
- Use short descriptive labels for regions (e.g., "us-west-2 (Oregon)") and avoid internal codes as primary.
- Ensure keyboard-only interactions for main wizard buttons; screen reader-friendly step descriptions.

Backlog (triaged items — title | priority | owner | estimate):
- Inline VPC correction edits (add route/sg) | P0 | Marcus Chen | 3d
- Background connectivity test that pings endpoints via ephemeral instance | P0 | Evan Liu | 5d
- HSM availability map (live data by region) in the wizard | P1 | Sofia Martinez | 4d
- Export audit bundle (YAML + support logs) | P0 | Aisha Patel | 2d
- Resume/setup state UI + resume tokens | P1 | Platform Eng | 5d
- Multi-account TGW UX variant | P2 | Product | 6d
- Add inline compliance text snippets (SOC2, FedRAMP notes) | P2 | Security | 2d

Open decisions (needs PM/Legal/Infra):
- Do we allow default key creation in customer KMS from the console (yes/no)? Security prefers explicit customer key creation.
- Required telemetry during private deployment for support: minimal metrics only or broader? (Privacy/legal input required).
- Support SLA for guided setup: what window and who is owner for out-of-hours installs?

Notes for handoff to solutions engineering:
- Bundle to include sample IAM policies with least privilege for the ephemeral validator job.
- Include a preflight checklist PDF to send to customers ahead of scheduled setup call.
- Provide runbook for common failures (CIDR overlap, missing internet egress, KMS permission denied).

Next steps and immediate asks: (for next groom)
- UX: produce 3 low-fidelity screens for BYOVPC flow and recommended-VPC flow (action: Marcus, due 2026-03-10)
- Infra: prototype ephemeral connectivity tester and return a minimal API contract (action: Evan, due 2026-03-17)
- Security: confirm policy on console key creation and telemetry (action: Sofia, due 2026-03-12)

Misc notes / scratch ideas:
- Consider a "dry-run" mode that simulates the deploy and generates a customer-facing checklist without making changes. Useful for security review loops.
- Autobudget suggestion: estimate monthly GPU token spend given declared qps and model family, show as optional toggle during capacity step.
- Post-deploy: seed the console with quick-start integrations (examples: chatbot demo in private network, embeddings batch job) to drive initial validation.

Attachments referenced: Confluence page PLATFORM-PRIVATE-ONBOARDING (architecture + runbooks), JIRA-PRIVDEP-87 (ephemeral tester), and prototype PR on GitHub (linked above).

Unresolved questions list (short):
- Should the wizard allow selecting cross-account roles or require a service account in target account?
- What exact logs/telemetry are permissible for automated health checks under customer contracts?
- How to present HSM procurement lead times in a way that doesn't block initial deploy?

End of doc (draft).
